source_acquisition.search_note: The automatic inventory row says no_public_source_found and the local visual-source directory is empty. The PDF exposes arXiv 2606.06085v1 and OpenReview n50Ipdt5d5 but no author code URL. Read-only gh exact-title repository search returned none; exact-title code search returned several audit/reproduction repositories. MachineLearning-Nerd/icml26-auction-revenue was accepted only after gh metadata showed homepage https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06085 and its README matched the exact title, authors, OpenReview id, and arXiv id. Its tree contains the exact paper TeX and all nine rendered PNG assets used in the PDF, but no plot script, source data, or author BM07 implementation, so the source is partial at visual-asset/TeX level rather than full plotting provenance.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Categorical saturated raster colors: red/blue/green/yellow parameter series, with red empirical/no-swap and blue theoretical overlays in CDF panels; Figure 1 adds a dark navy series. Line styles provide redundancy only for two-series theory/empirical overlays.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: All ten plot objects are embedded 640x480 raster PNGs with soft masks; LaTeX text, captions, axes surrounding text, and page layout remain vector PDF objects.
paper_style.style_consistency: Axes, labels, legend placement, palette, and dash conventions are highly consistent across the four numbered figures and six Appendix E panels. Appendix E has weaker caption consistency because its panels are unnumbered brace text, and Figure 4 duplicates Figure 3.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Time-averaged revenue for different values of v2.

color.semantic_mapping: red dash-dot=v2=0; yellow dotted=v2=0.2; blue dashed=v2=0.5; dark-blue dotted=v2=0.8; green dash-dot=v2=1.

encodings.line: dash-dot, dotted, and dashed series styles
encodings.text: axis labels, ticks, and lower-right legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Deterministic first-price auction with n=3, valuations (v1,v2,v3)=(1,v2,0), k=10, and v2 in {0,0.2,0.5,0.8,1}; x spans 0–300,000 rounds and y is time-average revenue on approximately 0–1. Each curve is a single trajectory. The text claims all cases exceed v2−0.1, but no threshold, seed, repeat count, uncertainty, or failure value is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: p.1 Question 1.1 (finite horizon) → pp.5 and 9 Theorem 2.6/Equation (3) → p.9 deterministic valuation sweep → Figure 1 → text claim that revenue surpasses v2−1/k. This is empirical main-comparison evidence, not a proof of the universal theorem.
design_strengths: A common round/revenue frame makes all five valuation cases directly comparable.
The legend maps each curve to v2 and the rapid transient plus separated plateaus are visible in one compact panel.
design_weaknesses: Five-way identity relies heavily on color and is not reliably grayscale-safe.
The claimed v2−0.1 benchmark is absent, and the tiny raster/sparse caption omit n, k, horizon, averaging, and replication details.
A single unreplicated trajectory gives no across-run stability information.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use one shared round/revenue frame for a controlled valuation sweep, but add a visibly labeled theorem threshold, non-color redundancy, and the full setup/replication definition to the caption.

evidence.label: Figure 1; p.9 lower-middle plot and caption

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Impact of discretization level k on revenue convergence.

color.semantic_mapping: red dash-dot=k=10; blue dashed=k=30; green dash-dot=k=50.

encodings.line: dash-dot for k=10/50 and dashed for k=30
encodings.text: axis labels, ticks, and lower-right legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Deterministic n=3 auction with valuations (1,1,0), k in {10,30,50}, x spanning 0–300,000 rounds and y approximately 0.6–1.0. The intended comparison is higher apparent long-run revenue but slower convergence for larger k. No target/reference line, seed, repeat, uncertainty, or exact convergence criterion is reported.
figures.evidence_relation: Equation (3) and Corollary 2.7 motivate k dependence (pp.5 and 9) → p.9 controlled (1,1,0) setup → Figure 2 → p.10 statement that larger k raises long-run revenue at a slower rate and empirical convergence is faster than the theory rate.
design_strengths: Identical axes expose the speed/limit trade-off without panel changes.
Three simple paths and short legend labels keep the comparison readable.
design_weaknesses: No theorem/target reference or convergence-time marker is drawn.
Red and green share dash-dot styling, so color remains necessary; the caption omits the valuation profile, bidders, horizon, and main finding.
No repeated-run or uncertainty evidence is shown.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show discretization as a common-axis trajectory comparison, while adding explicit target/reference lines and a predeclared convergence measure.

evidence.label: Figure 2; p.10 upper plot and caption

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Revenue produced for different number of bidders.

color.semantic_mapping: blue dashed=n=2; green dash-dot=n=4; red dash-dot=n=3; yellow dash-dot=n=5.

encodings.text: axis labels, ticks, and lower-right legend

figures.data_and_statistics: i.i.d. binary Bayesian valuations vi in {0,1} with probability 1/2, k=10, n in {2,3,4,5}; the intended target is E[v2]=1−(n+1)2^(-n). x spans 0–100,000 rounds and y 0–1. Each line is a time-average revenue trajectory; bidders run parallel no-swap learners for the two realised values. Expected-value baselines, repetitions, seeds, and uncertainty are absent.
figures.evidence_relation: p.2 Claim 1.7 and p.9 Section 4 motivate finite-time revenue → p.9 binary Bayesian setup and E[v2] target → Figure 3 → p.10 qualitative claim that revenue approaches E[v2]. The deterministic dual-fitting theorem is not a Bayesian theorem.
design_strengths: One common axis makes bidder-count-dependent plateaus easy to compare.
The compact legend exposes the population-size sweep and the initial transient.
design_weaknesses: Expected E[v2] baselines are only implicit in prose, not drawn.
Color is the primary series identity channel; the caption omits the i.i.d. distribution, k, target, and main finding.
No replication or uncertainty distinguishes a trajectory from a robust estimate.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a discrete population-size sweep with one common revenue axis, and draw the analytically computed target for every series.

evidence.label: Figure 3; p.10 middle plot and caption

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: Revenue produced for different number of bidders.

color.semantic_mapping: blue dashed=n=2; green dash-dot=n=4; red dash-dot=n=3; yellow dash-dot=n=5; identical to Figure 3.

encodings.text: axis labels, ticks, and lower-right legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Appendix E repeats the i.i.d. binary Bayesian setup of Figure 3: vi in {0,1} with probability 1/2, n in {2,3,4,5}, k=10, and the E[v2]=1−(n+1)2^(-n) target. The exact 640×480 reve1.png asset is reused; this is not an independent run or parameter slice, and no uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: p.10 says fuller Bayesian figures/explanation are deferred to Appendix E → p.23 repeats the main binary Bayesian revenue object → subsequent p.24 CDF panels provide conditional-strategy detail. Figure 4 is appendix support/reproduction, not an additional Bayesian proof or independent replication.
design_strengths: Places the revenue display next to the detailed Appendix E setup.
Exact asset reuse makes the main/appendix link easy to verify.
design_weaknesses: It duplicates Figure 3 without new information, uncertainty, target annotation, or a changed slice.
The sparse caption remains non-self-contained and color-dependent, so the appendix placement adds little visual evidence.
figures.reusable_pattern: Repeat a headline plot in an appendix only when the appendix version adds independent detail, uncertainty, or a controlled slice; otherwise link to the original and spend space on the missing evidence.

figures.label: Unnumbered CDF panel: v1=0
figures.module: Appendix E / binary Bayesian / conditional CDF

caption.text: Time-averaged CDF played by bidder 1 once v1 = 0.

encodings.text: axis labels, ticks, and lower-right legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Binary Bayesian n=2 setting with k=50 and T=10^4, bidder 1 conditioned on v1=0. The empirical CDF is one across the plotted bid domain, consistent with always bidding zero. No point-mass marker, replicate distribution, or uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: p.23 Appendix E defines the binary Bayesian experiment and states that zero-value bidders always bid zero → p.24 first panel gives direct qualitative evidence for the v1=0 conditional behavior. It is not a theorem/proof or a quantitative CDF-distance test.
design_strengths: The conditional behavior is immediately visible on shared Bid/CDF axes.
A one-series panel avoids legend overload and is grayscale-readable.
design_weaknesses: A flat CDF at one is visually trivial and does not show the point mass/step at bid zero.
No theory comparator or sample count appears; the unnumbered brace caption makes cross-reference difficult.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a conditional CDF panel for a degenerate strategy only when the point mass and conditioning are explicitly marked, preferably with a companion non-degenerate comparison.

evidence.label: Unnumbered panel; p.24 upper plot with brace caption

figures.label: Unnumbered CDF panel: v1=1
figures.module: Appendix E / binary Bayesian / conditional CDF

caption.text: Time-averaged CDF played by bidder 1 once v1 = 1.

color.semantic_mapping: blue dashed=1/(1-x)-1 Bayes Mixed Nash theory; red dash-dot=no-swap dynamics empirical CDF.

encodings.line: blue dashed theory; red dash-dot no-swap
encodings.text: axis labels, ticks, formula legend, and lower-right legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Binary Bayesian n=2, continuous bid domain [0,1] for the equilibrium comparison, discretization k=50 and T=10^4, conditioned on v1=1. The analytic CDF F_P(x)=1/(1−x)−1 rises through its support to x=1/2 and then plateaus; the empirical no-swap CDF overlays it. No CDF-distance statistic, repetitions, or uncertainty is supplied.
figures.evidence_relation: p.23 gives the Bayes Mixed Nash analytic CDF and k=50,T=10^4 setting → p.24 second panel overlays the stated target with time-average bidding → supports the qualitative “very close” claim, not a Bayesian equilibrium proof.
design_strengths: Direct theory/empirical overlay uses identical axes.
Dashed versus dash-dot provides non-color redundancy, and the support cutoff is visible.
design_weaknesses: Legend omits support/domain and no discrepancy metric is reported.
No uncertainty or sample denominator; tiny labels and an unnumbered brace caption weaken stand-alone interpretation.
figures.reusable_pattern: Overlay an analytic distribution and empirical CDF with distinct line styles, but report support, sampling unit, replicate variability, and a scalar discrepancy beside the plot.

evidence.label: Unnumbered panel; p.24 lower plot with brace caption

figures.label: Unnumbered revenue panel

encodings.text: axis labels, ticks, and lower-right legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Three-value Bayesian n=2 setting with P(0)=0.25, P(0.5)=0.25, P(1)=0.5 and k=30. Appendix E prose says T=50000, while the plotted x-axis extends to 500000; this is a source/text horizon mismatch. The text gives E[v2]≈0.4026, but no target line, replicate, uncertainty, or convergence criterion is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: p.23 introduces the three-value distribution and expected second-highest value → p.25 revenue panel supplies the qualitative convergence component of the Bayesian extension. The main deterministic theorem does not cover this case.
design_strengths: The plateau is easy to see on an uncluttered common revenue axis.
A single series keeps the diagnostic legible.
design_weaknesses: The prose/axis horizon mismatch (T=50000 versus x-axis through 500000) is unresolved.
The expected target is not drawn, and one trajectory without uncertainty cannot support a strong convergence claim.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep a single trajectory only as a diagnostic, but align text and axis horizons and add a target line plus a predeclared convergence/error summary.

figures.data_and_statistics: Three-value Bayesian n=2 setting with probabilities P(0)=0.25, P(0.5)=0.25, P(1)=0.5, k=30, and prose T=50000. Bidder 1 is conditioned on v1=0; the empirical CDF is flat at one, consistent with always bidding zero. No point-mass annotation, repeat count, or uncertainty is present.
figures.evidence_relation: p.23 defines the three-value Bayesian extension → p.25 zero-value panel supplies the degenerate conditional-strategy component of the Appendix E conclusion that empirical distributions follow the Bayes Mixed Nash Equilibrium. It is qualitative evidence only.
design_strengths: It uses the same axes and red empirical convention as the binary zero-value panel.
The conditional strategy is easy to scan in the panel set.
design_weaknesses: The degenerate CDF is visually uninformative without an explicit atom/step at zero.
It omits the shared experiment settings and inherits the unresolved horizon context; the unnumbered caption limits reuse.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show degenerate conditional distributions with an explicit atom/step and a shared caption that binds all panels to the experiment.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 sweeps deterministic v2, Figure 2 shows the k/revenue-speed trade-off, Figures 3–4 show binary Bayesian revenue by n, and the Appendix E conditional CDF panels compare observed strategies with Bayes Mixed Nash formulas. The plots are downstream qualitative evidence for a theory-led paper whose LP/dual-fitting mechanism stays in text and equations.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Numbered captions use a short quantity-for-parameter sentence and omit most setup, encoding, uncertainty, and findings. Appendix E uses unnumbered brace text under each image, with no shared caption for the composite panel sets.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: No tables occur in the 25-page PDF, so there is no table-header system to audit.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Algorithm 1 defines repeated auction interaction and Section 3 derives the LP/dual-fitting guarantee; Figures 1–3 provide deterministic/Bayesian result diagnostics. There is no component ablation, and the Bayesian plots are outside the proved deterministic theorem boundary.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: p.10 explicitly defers Bayesian figures and explanation to Appendix E. Figure 4 is the same reve1 asset as Figure 3; Appendix E then adds conditional CDF overlays and a three-value setting rather than independent replication.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Raster plot labels are consistently small DejaVu-Sans-like text and PDF captions/body are Computer Modern; typography is stable across main and appendix objects but plot text is below comfortable single-column reading size.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Red/blue/green/yellow recur as parameter-series colors, red is empirical/no-swap in CDFs, and blue is theory in overlays. Multi-series trajectory figures still rely primarily on color and are not grayscale-safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Common-axis trajectory sweeps for controlled v2, k, and n comparisons.
Direct analytic-versus-empirical CDF overlays with distinct dash styles.
A compact appendix panel set for conditional strategies, when each panel shares a fully specified experiment caption.
highest_value_objects: Figure 2: revenue/convergence trade-off across discretization levels.
p.24 v1=1 CDF overlay: the clearest direct comparison of the stated Bayes Mixed Nash target with empirical bidding.
failure_patterns: No error bars, bands, repetitions, or quantitative CDF discrepancy.
Absent theorem/expected-value reference lines and color-heavy legends.
Unnumbered appendix panels and a literal Figure 3/Figure 4 duplicate.
p.25 prose/axis horizon mismatch: T=50000 in text versus an x-axis through 500000.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use small, consistent raster trajectory and CDF panels as qualitative evidence that no-swap-regret revenue and conditional bidding approach deterministic or Bayes Mixed Nash targets, while keeping the principal theorem and proof in text and formulas.
